Five of Chelsea's most memorable moments against Sunderland
news.body_en: Sunderland may have only been an opponent of ours in just over half of the Premier League seasons to date, but the Black Cats have been on the receiving end of some iconic Chelsea moments. We first played Sunderland in the Premier League in 1996/97, recording a memorable 6-2 victory at Stamford Bridge. Since then, there have been goals, performances and top-flight title celebrations that will live long in the memory. Here we bring you the top five… Chelsea 4-0 Sunderland7 August 1999 The sun was shining at Stamford Bridge as Chelsea, tipped for the title by some, started the new season in style by sinking newly-promoted Sunderland. Gus Poyet, Gianfranco Zola and Tore Andre Flo had already given us an unassailable lead when Poyet bagged the goal of the game. Zola scooped the ball over the Mackems’ defence and into the path of Poyet, who expertly scissor-kicked his volley into the top corner. In creation and execution, it was simply sublime. Chelsea 7-2 Sunderland16 January 2010 In a season full of goals, Ashley Cole’s against Sunderland at the turn of the year was voted by supporters as the best, and it was easy to see why. From inside his own half, John Terry put a lofted first-time pass into the path of the marauding left-back. Running at full tilt didn’t stop Cole bringing the ball under his spell with an immaculate first touch. As Sunderland skipper Lorik Cana slid across to block the shot, Cole calmly cut the ball inside him before using the outside of his left boot to find the far corner. Sunderland 3-4 Chelsea4 December 2013 Singling out one Eden Hazard performance for Chelsea is no easy task, but his display at the Stadium of Light in December 2013 arguably stands above the rest. After providing an assist for Frank Lampard, Hazard netted two individual goals of the highest quality to help us to a 4-3 win. His second goal, again after combining with Lampard, was particularly magical. He instinctively and ecstatically ripped off his shirt in celebration, a sure sign even the cool Belgian was impressed by his masterclass on Wearside. Chelsea 3-1 Sunderland24 May 2015 Both of our most recent Premier League trophy lifts have come after final-day victories over Sunderland at Stamford Bridge. The first was in May 2015, when a penalty from Diego Costa and a Loic Remy brace secured a 3-1 success after we had gone behind early. One of the many highlights that day was the sight of Didier Drogba being carried off the pitch by his team-mates after his final Chelsea appearance. History would repeat itself two years later… Chelsea 5-1 SunderlandMay 21 2017 On that occasion, it was John Terry who was celebrated off the Stamford Bridge turf 26 minutes into his final game, which would prove a resounding victory over the relegated Black Cats. Again, we went behind. Again, we hit back in style. Willian levelled with an angle finish before goals from Eden Hazard and Pedro, two of the stars of the season, had us in control as the contest drew to a close. Michy Batshuayi, whose goal at West Brom a week earlier secured the title, added a late double as the celebrations started in earnest once more.

news.title: Erin Cuthbert: 'There will be a reaction'
news.body_en: Chelsea captain Erin Cuthbert reflected on a disappointing stalemate against Everton on Saturday afternoon, but vowed the side would bounce back against Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday. The skipper started the match for only the second time this season after recovering from a knee injury sustained in the summer and was substituted for Aggie Beever-Jones after 74 minutes with the Blues chasing a goal. Despite our best efforts, it was not to be, and Cuthbert gave her thoughts after the final whistle. She said: 'We did really well at getting ourselves ahead in the first half. That’s been our target: to score early, and then we conceded an unfortunate goal, which is no one’s fault. But we need to do a little bit more. 'We weren’t quite on the same page today defensively. We weren’t pressing as a group, as we have done in the previous games. We were a bit sloppy on the ball, too. 'But I can’t fault anybody’s effort. The effort has been there. It’s just one of those days where we were really not at it, and we can’t have too many of those if we want to be in a title race.' The teams went in with the scores at 1-1 during the interval after a Lucy Bronze own goal had cancelled out Sandy Baltimore's opener. Everton could then afford to sit back during the second half, meaning Chelsea were stuck trying to find a winner. 'You can’t get too stressed,' Cuthbert explained. 'I feel like as players we tend to look at scoreboards and things start to slip away. But you’ll always get a chance, and we had a few half-chances here and there today. We were dangerous on set pieces. We obviously scored from Katie's (McCabe) cross as well. 'But you have games where you just grind out results. You don’t always have to be at your best throughout the whole season, as long as you’re getting the results. But we didn’t have that today, and we can’t have too many more of those.' There is very little time for the team to linger over today's result, with a trip to Sweden on the horizon and a game against Hacken on Tuesday night. As captain, Cuthbert will take responsibility for lifting the spirits and making sure we are ready for that challenge, before returning to Stamford Bridge to face Manchester City next weekend. 'There’s going to be a reaction, for sure,' she said. 'There’s a lot of unhappy people in the dressing room, and rightly so, because this is a club that expects to win games of football. But just the quality was lacking for us today, myself included. If we all looked at ourselves in the dressing room, we all know that we could have done a lot better today. 'I’m sure that we’ll be back at training tomorrow, ready and fully focused on Hacken. We will make sure that we put our best foot forward come Tuesday night.'

news.title: Alonso on Lavia’s ‘brain for the team’ and his next step
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has emphasised Romeo Lavia's growing importance in his Chelsea side, highlighting the midfielder's recent development while insisting there is still more to come. Lavia was excellent in our previous two matches, against Liverpool and Manchester United, with the added bonus that he completed the 90 minutes in both. It has reinforced the belief that Lavia is establishing himself as a key controller in the heart of our midfield, and that consistency and rhythm is something Alonso knows from personal experience will only help his team. ‘I always have the feeling that every time the midfield area works, the team works better,’ Alonso said. ‘Romeo is in a very good place, not just the last game. I think that for the last month he's been very consistent in his performance. ‘He's been very important for the team because in the middle you need to have a brain for yourself, but a brain for the team. He's good with the ball, he's giving balance, and he's connecting really well with the players around him. ‘It's not rocket science to know that once you have good midfielders, the team normally looks better.’ Despite Lavia’s eye-catching displays, our manager has made it clear he will continue to demand higher standards from the Belgian international to ensure his ceiling is reached. He said: ‘We need to push him. We need to help him continue so he can take the next step, because it’s not enough yet. ‘There's been a change, and he knows that,’ added Alonso when asked if Lavia is doing anything differently. ‘He has realised that's the way.’

news.title: Frustrated Bompastor: 'We were not clinical or ruthless enough'
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor was left feeling frustrated by our 1-1 draw with Everton at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon, but felt it was an opportunity to reflect and improve before Tuesday night's Women's Champions League trip to Hacken in Sweden. The head coach said in her pre-match press conference the Toffees would be hard to break down, and that proved to be true until Sandy Baltimore broke the deadlock after 28 minutes. Yet an unfortunate own goal from Lucy Bronze levelled things up almost immediately afterwards, and Chelsea were once again forced to battle through their block. While Chelsea's unbeaten run in the WSL was extended to 17 games, and we remain undefeated in all competitions this season, Bompastor took the opportunity to reflect on the draw after the game and pointed to the areas where she felt her side were below par this afternoon. 'The result is really frustrating for us,' she said. 'Today the performance was not good enough for us to get a better result. We were probably too slow. We had 20 shots on goal, eight on target, but even when we shot on target we were not clinical enough, not ruthless enough, and I don’t think we made Everton's goalkeeper work hard enough. 'Also, the connection between the players didn’t really click today. So it happens. When we have a performance like that, it’s good for us to provide feedback and to be honest and realistic about what happened on the pitch. 'In terms of the defensive aspects, today we were not compact enough as a block. We didn’t recover enough balls in terms of the high press. So that’s something we need to do better going into the next game. 'Without the ball, we conceded an unfortunate goal, but it was the goal that allowed them to get a point from this game. So it happens sometimes. As much as we are frustrated, now it’s for us to analyse the game, take the feedback, and move on to the next one.' Despite the initial disappointment of dropping points, the head coach did point to some positives to take from the game. Chelsea kept Everton to zero shots on target throughout the 90 minutes, even if we struggled to break through their low block. And with a match against Hacken to play on Tuesday night, there's no time to dwell on today's result. 'If we analyse from the beginning of the season, we had many games where we had a lot of good performances and a lot of quality on the pitch,' she continued. 'So it’s good for us when we are doing well not to go too high and when we have a frustrating result, not to go too low. Because I believe this team has a lot of quality, and we can do better than what we did today. 'Sometimes it's good not to always perform at a good level because it means you still have work to be done, and you need that. For me, it’s best when you have a frustrating result to play quickly straight afterwards. So the quick turnaround is actually a positive thing. You can quickly move on and focus on what is next.'

news.title: Match report: Chelsea Women 1-1 Everton
news.body_en: With a defensive record only bettered by Chelsea in the WSL this season, the Blues knew we would be in for a tough afternoon against Everton even before the match had kicked off, and so it proved as we had to settle for a point at Stamford Bridge. After a cagey first half hour, Sandy Baltimore broke the deadlock when a small connection on the ball saw her steer home from a Lucy Bronze header back across goal. It felt like Chelsea were on our way, but when Bronze took an unfortunate touch from a looping ball in, the Toffees were back on level terms just four minutes later, and the teams went in at 1-1 at the break. Despite Everton not managing a shot on target during the match, the visitors made things really difficult for the Blues, reducing us to half-chances throughout. Their efforts were rewarded as they kept us from adding to the scoreline and took a point away from the Bridge. Sonia Bompastor made four alterations to her starting XI, swapping Veerle Buurman, Nathalie Bjorn and Sjoeke Nusken for Bronze, Kadeisha Buchanan and Erin Cuthbert. Lauren James had unfortunately been ruled out with a hamstring injury earlier in the week, and Wieke Kaptein came into the line-up in her place. The head coach had mentioned in her pre-match press conference that she expected the visitors to defend well, and that's exactly what happened in the opening stages of the game as the Toffees played in a compact formation as they attempted to negate our strengths. Our first real attempt came from one of Ellie Carpenter's trademark runs down the flank, and as she let fly with a shot, only a tiny deflection from the defender saw it bounce just wide of the right-hand post. Melvine Malard was next to go close with a header that was just off target, but the offside flag went up soon afterwards to confirm that it wouldn't have counted. It wasn't going to be easy to break Everton down, but the Blues were getting closer. After a superb one-two with Carpenter, Kaptein blasted her shot towards goal but had her attempt cleared off the line. Our opener came soon afterwards. After we took a short corner, Katie McCabe swung a cross into the back post to find the head of Bronze. The centre-back cushioned her header across the face of goal, allowing Baltimore to nod home with the slightest of touches. Yet the Toffees hit back when a looping cross from Yuka Momiki took an unfortunate touch off Bronze and deflected into the back of the net. Our number 22 almost cancelled out the own goal with a bullet header seven minutes before the break, but an impressive stop saw Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan tip the attempt over the bar. After another tight opening to the second half, Bompastor made a double substitution after 55 minutes, introducing Nusken and Thompson for Baltimore and Kaptein. The clock ticked towards 70 and, other than a series of corners, the Blues were yet to put any real pressure on a resolute Everton defence. When the Blues were awarded a free-kick for a late challenge on Carpenter, McCabe took it short to Thompson just outside her, and the American laid the ball off to Walsh. The midfielder bent in a curling shot, but Brosnan was able to collect. That was the only real danger we caused in the second half as the statistics showed we fired 21 shots on goal but ended the match with only three big chances created. It was a frustrating day, but we will look to regain top spot when we face leaders Manchester City next weekend in the WSL. We drop to second in the table, two points behind leaders Manchester City, following their 5-0 win over West Ham United earlier today. We travel to Sweden to face Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, with kick-off set for 5.45pm UK time. We will then back at Stamford Bridge for our top-of-the-table clash with Man City next Saturday. Tickets are still available and you can secure your place here. news.title: U18 Premier League Cup report: Chelsea Under-18s 3-1 Charlton Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s are through to the quarter-finals of the U18 Premier League Cup following a 3-1 victory over Charlton Athletic. Andrew Pennie won us a spot-kick which Jashayde Greenwood coolly converted to give us the lead. Greenwood returned the favour 14 minutes later, setting up Pennie’s goal which put us back in front after Charlton’s Jayden Twum equalised in the 28th minute. The Blues pushed for a third in the second 45 minutes and our persistence soon told as we earned and converted another penalty through Greenwood. In the first half it was all Chelsea and it didn’t take long for us to take the lead. Pennie was played through on the left wing with two defenders still to beat. He cut inside, drawing a foul from the Charlton defender, leaving the referee with no choice but to point to the penalty spot. Greenwood stepped up to take and made no mistake, going hard and low into the bottom right corner while sending the goalkeeper the wrong way. The visitors responded with a goal of their own, as Twum managed to get half a yard on Jacob Hall before tucking the ball into the far corner. We regained the lead quickly, as Greenwood became the creator and Pennie the goalscorer. The former received the ball and opted to drive down towards the byline; he then cut his pass across the face of goal to Pennie, who thumped the ball against the crossbar and in to make it 2-1 before the break. After the interval, we came racing out the blocks once more, aiming to extend our advantage to ensure our spot in the last eight. We enjoyed the best opportunities of the half through Heze Grimwade and Kwamina Ampah. First, Grimwade was played through one-on-one with the goalkeeper by Greenwood but dragged his shot wide. Minutes after coming on Ampah was presented with the golden chance to settle the match as Gabriel Sambou dinked a cross into the penalty area, but Ampah’s shot was off target. Charlton put some pressure on us too, but we handled the heat well and stood firm. Josh Henry in particular denied the visitors another equaliser with two lunging challenges to turn goal-bound efforts out for a corner. The Blues eventually got their third, and it was from the spot once again as Greenwood remained composed to net his brace. We earned the penalty when Emmanuel Ayinde headed Grimwade’s cross towards goal, only to be denied by the hand of Raynon Richman. Greenwood elected for a different spot-kick approach this time; he stuttered and waited for Williams to move before smashing his strike into the opposite corner. This win means that we are through to the knockout stages of the Under-18 Premier League Cup. Chelsea Under-18s host Arsenal in the Under-18 Premier League on Saturday 21 November at Cobham Training Ground. The game gets underway at 11am GMT and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Penders on learning quickly, that Mbeumo save and dreaming big
news.body_en: By his own admission, Mike Penders has experienced a ‘rollercoaster of emotions’ during his start to life between the posts at Chelsea. It is to his credit how he has handled the ups and downs thrown at him so far. Penders started the season as our number two, behind Emiliano Martinez in the pecking order. He made his Blues debut in the Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town in August and started the next round, too, as Leeds United were beaten 6-3. But the tall Belgian was thrust into the spotlight when Martinez sustained a nasty jaw injury midway through the second half of our Premier League game at Everton. Penders helped see out the clean sheet, making a positive first impression in the English top flight. However, the following weekend, it was Penders’ own goal that set Tottenham on their way to a rare victory at Stamford Bridge. That mistake was a test of the 21-year-old’s nerve, but his response was emphatic. He put in two stellar performances against Liverpool and Manchester United, with several saves plucked from the very top drawer. There is certainly plenty for Penders to reflect on as he sits down at Cobham ahead of our trip to Sunderland this weekend. ‘Right now I feel very good,’ he says. ‘It’s been a rollercoaster of emotions as well, but now I’m very happy I could react positively in the last two games. ‘When it comes to pressure, I try to stay as relaxed as possible. And then, of course, mistakes happen. You think about them, that’s normal, but I try to turn it into something positive. I try to learn about it. I like to look at the videos to see what I could do better, and then move on. ‘It was a learning moment, and outside of the mistake, I felt okay during the game. The most important thing was to have a positive reaction in the next couple of games, and I’m happy I could bring that.’ Penders benefitted from having his whole family in attendance at the Tottenham game. Afterwards, they offered support, of course, but were also able to take his mind off it by changing the subject when required. Penders also felt the love from his team-mates and his manager, Xabi Alonso. ‘He spoke very positively about me during interviews, which gave me a lot of confidence to go into the next game. Also, my defenders and some of the other players came up to me and just spoke with me. I appreciated that a lot. ‘You don’t forget these kinds of things, you know? The players who come up to you, write you a little message: "Keep your head up, keep going.” It means a lot.’ Any goalkeeper plays on the margins. A small error can be brutally punished. On the flip side, a pivotal save can preserve three points. It comes with the territory. Just seven days after his own goal, Penders made such a brilliant stop it has been nominated for the Premier League Save of the Month award. You can vote for Mike’s improbable fingertip stop from Bryan Mbeumo’s rasping volley here. It was a save so good that it needed multiple replays and camera angles to prove Penders had actually got a decisive touch on the ball. He reveals it was a source of mirth among his team-mates afterwards. ‘The ball came so quickly, I didn’t even see it properly,’ says Penders. ‘It was just instinct, pure instinct; a reaction. I felt a good touch on my fingertips, and after that moment, I screamed all the positive emotions out. I had to. I was so happy with that moment. ‘Then, after the game, no-one believed me that I touched it! I was like, “Yeah, I touched it; you will see afterwards”. ‘Then it was pretty quickly on Twitter. A team-mate came into the dressing room saying: “He touched it”. I was very happy it was a good angle because if the angle wasn't right, they could still have some doubts!’ Mike Penders' reaction time 🤯🔵 @ChelseaFC pic.twitter.com/5aXNDl8zwd Penders is flattered by comparisons to his compatriot Thibaut Courtois, which serve as motivation to work even harder. His focus now is on trying to write his own story and make a name for himself. He knows one way to do that is to learn from those around him. Martinez – ‘a very good guy’ – has already proven to be a huge help, and there are certain elements of the Argentinean’s game that Penders is trying to implement in his own, as he sees fit. Combine those Cobham learnings with invaluable Premier League experience and you sense Penders’ trajectory is rising. It gives him hope he can realise his ambitions, even if he knows there is a long way to go. ‘I have a lot of dreams...a lot of dreams. I hope I can win as many trophies as possible with the club. ‘The big dream? I think that would be winning the Champions League or winning a World Cup with my country, something like that. And then maybe go for the biggest individual prizes. ‘These are dreams that are far away, but you want to work towards them. This is the start of the journey.’

news.title: Confirmed Chelsea Women line up vs Everton
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has made four changes to her Chelsea side for our Women's Super League match against Everton at Stamford Bridge this afternoon. Following our 6-0 win against Charlton last Sunday, Bompastor had almost a week to prepare for today's home match against Everton. Captain Erin Cuthbert starts in midfield in place of Sjoeke Nusken, while Wieke Kaptein comes in for Lauren James, who sustained a hamstring injury at The Valley last weekend and has been ruled out until the end of the current block of fixtures. news.title: Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Everton press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our Women's Super League clash against Everton on Saturday, and here are the key talking points from what the Blues head coach said. We remain unbeaten this season after 13 matches, but Bompastor assured that the standard of preparation will be as high as always as we head into our fifth WSL game of the campaign at Stamford Bridge. The head coach reported that Lauren James will be missing until the end of this block of matches before the international break, after a scan confirmed that she sustained a hamstring injury during the 6-0 win over Charlton last weekend. Lexi Potter, meanwhile, is available again. Here are the rest of the key talking points from our head coach’s pre-match press conference on Friday. 'My role is to make sure that when we are in good form, we don't go too high. And sometimes when things are not going the way we want, we don't go too low either. I'm responsible for that. 'Right now, of course, we are happy with the results and most of the performances we are having on the pitch, but we won't change anything. We keep working hard, we keep the same mentality, we train with intensity, and we come into every game as well prepared as we can. 'That's what we need to do. Every game in this league is so important and so difficult, so we need to make sure we sustain that for as long as possible.' 'It's always difficult to score goals against any team. The difference maybe in the Charlton game was that we scored early on the game, and we were winning 4-0 after 19 minutes. And when you are really efficient and clinical from the beginning, it changes the whole game. 'Going into the game tomorrow, we are expecting it might not be possible for us to achieve. They are a really difficult team to break down, and we will have to play at our best if we want to get a result from the game. We'll try our best to break them down, to score as early as possible in the game and to see how they react. 'They haven't conceded many goals, and they are an aggressive team, but in a good way. They had a good result against Manchester United, so I'm sure they are coming in with confidence as well. We are very much aware of the threats and the quality this Everton side has, especially in terms of the defensive aspects.' 'It's really important to be hungry. The hunger is part of the mentality and the mindset a team have, and that's what makes the difference between the good teams and the great teams, the ones who are able to win trophies. 'Sometimes you don't always play the best football, but you always find a way to win games, and that's really important. We focus a lot on the quality of the performance we want to put on the pitch, but some days it's not always possible for different reasons. We need to make sure when those days come, we have that hunger and that mentality to turn things around even when it's not the way we want to play.' 'Ellie has been starting her actions higher up the pitch for sure, and also she probably feels more freedom to attack. She's been working really hard in training sessions, and she stays at the end to do some extra work around finishing in the box, crosses, the quality of the crosses, scanning, and the quality of her first touch. 'She's always keen to work hard, and she always asks for extras. She's been doing that from the beginning of the season, and it's paying off, so it's good for her.' 'Everyone could see that it was Lucy (Bronze). She was really good at scaring people. She got me, but she also got most people in the team. But it was really nice. 'We work really hard most of the time, and we spend so much time focusing on every detail. We speak a lot about our ambitions, how we want to perform on the pitch, and we are professional, so we do that one hundred per cent. 'But it's also good when you can find a good balance and have good laughs and some fun. At the end of the day, football is a game, and when your team is able to play at their best, it's when players have fun on the pitch.' news.title: Alonso wants Chelsea focused on the pitch, not the table
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso insists it is still much too early to be reading anything from the Premier League table, both in terms of his Chelsea team’s progress and the quality of opponent we will face against Sunderland. The Blues head to the Stadium of Light for our next Premier League fixture, taking on Sunderland in a 2pm kick-off on Sunday. A quick glance at the league table would suggest the two teams go into the game in very different fortunes. With three wins from our four Premier League matches since the last international break, Chelsea sit fourth in the table, with a chance to move up to third this weekend. Meanwhile, the Black Cats are stuck in the bottom spot, with just one league win to their name in 2026/27. However, our manager insisted he isn’t thinking about the league table at this stage of the campaign, when asked in his pre-match press conference if Chelsea’s position was a sign of our progress so far this season under his leadership. ‘The table means not too much because that can change so much in one week, in two games,’ Alonso pointed out. ‘We are taking a step forward, I think, with the ball, against the ball, being more solid. ‘We have a tough opponent, a tough visit to Sunderland, we know what it takes to win there. We know how demanding it will be. ‘The table doesn’t matter. I think that they deserve more points than they’ve got and it's going to be a tough away game.’ Instead, it is the task of building the consistency and momentum needed to be challenging in the upper reaches of the Premier League come May which is taking up Alonso and his team’s attention. That continues at Sunderland on Sunday, when the Blues will attempt to follow up last week’s 2-0 victory over Manchester United by making it back-to-back wins in the Premier League. ‘As I've said, it’s early days to talk too much about the table. We won the last game, now the focus is to keep winning, winning, winning and to build this mentality to go game by game. ‘We are expecting a tough game on Sunday against a team that do many good things. They should have more points probably and it is not going to be easy, for sure.’

Sunderland vs Chelsea: All you need to know
news.body_en: With almost a quarter of the Premier League campaign completed, fourth-placed Chelsea travel to the Stadium of Light. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to Sunday's 2pm kick-off against Sunderland. It will be the Blues’ first appearance in this time slot since our 4-3 beating of Brighton & Hove Albion and is a consequence of the Black Cats’ UEFA Europa League involvement on Thursday. Ebullient when Chelsea lost 2-1 there in May, Sunderland supporters are nervy in November, with five losses in six league outings and no three-point haul since August. As the final international break of 2026 looms, they lie bottom of the Premier League pile, two points from safety with the second-worst goal difference in the division. For their Europa League game in midweek, Regis Le Bris rotated six of the 11 who started last weekend’s 3-1 loss to fellow relegation fighters Coventry City. Previously unbeaten in the competition, they lost 2-0 at home to Dinamo Zagreb. Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso’s team had a free midweek to rest and prepare, following Saturday's second-half 2-0 dismantling of Manchester United, and will rise to third with a win on Wearside, should Brighton fail to beat Brentford. Speaking in his pre-match press conference, Alonso revealed that he will make a late decision on Sunday to determine if Moises Caicedo and Emiliano Martinez have recovered sufficiently to feature against Sunderland. Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix and Joao Pedro remain unavailable until at least the end of the forthcoming international break. ‘On Saturday we have our last training session before Sunday and we will decide,' Alonso replied when asked about Martinez. 'But he is training well. It is very good that Emi has made a great effort to be back and is ahead of the plan to be part of the team. So we will check and then on Sunday we will take the final decision. ‘Moi had little problems after the last game, so we expect to check on Saturday on different situations and he is one of them.' It may surprise Chelsea fans scarred by historic cup losses at Sunderland to hear that the Blues have a decent league record there. We have won 34 per cent of our 61 trips to this part of the North-East, just four fewer than our 38 per cent success rate at Tottenham Hotspur. Even before Roker Park closed its turnstiles in 1997, Chelsea had enjoyed sporadic success there, including a classic 2-0 victory in which Mickey Thomas scored from the spot soon after the restart and Kerry Dixon sealed the points late on. That was the first time we had ever won at Roker by two or more goals and remains our joint-biggest margin of victory at Sunderland. A run of just one top-flight defeat and no draws against the Black Cats between 2002 and 2013 weighs in heavily on that wins statistic, and the sole loss in that run came at Stamford Bridge. The spree of nine straight wins at the Stadium of Light included two memorably high-scoring clashes. A goalless first half did not foretell what was to happen after the break there on the last day of the 2008/09 season, a week before Guus Hiddink’s men would beat Everton in the FA Cup final. Nicolas Anelka broke the deadlock early in the second half with a spectacular drive from distance (to secure the Golden Boot), before Kieran Richardson made Petr Cech pay for a rare mishandling. The game swung again when Salomon Kalou lashed into the corner and Ashley Cole netted his second for the club to make it 3-1.  In the last minute, Kenwyne Jones pulled another one back for the relegation-threatened Wearsiders, and news filtered through that Newcastle United had lost to Aston Villa and would suffer the drop instead. Two years later, in February 2011, Phil Bardsley’s solo effort struck an early blow for the hosts, but minutes later Ahmed Elmohamady fouled Cole and Frank Lampard equalised from 12 yards. Anelka then pounced on a loose ball to feed Kalou, who edged Carlo Ancelotti’s defending champions ahead for the first time. The Black Cats kept scrapping and Richardson fired a free-kick through the Blues’ wall to send the two teams in level at the break. Chelsea continued to pepper Craig Gordon’s goal and when the keeper parried Lampard’s lashed shot, John Terry forced it home.  Before the final whistle, Anelka struck to seal an impressive 4-2 victory. Our most recent win at the home of the Mackems came in mid-December 2016, under Antonio Conte. The league leaders remained top over Christmas for the fifth time in the Premier League, thanks to Cesc Fabregas’ swept finish. Following his success against Manchester United, Cole Palmer has scored 19 of his 21 Premier League penalties for Chelsea. Only Frank Lampard (41 from 48) has managed a higher total. Romeo Lavia won possession 14 times during Saturday’s win, the most by any Chelsea player in a Premier League game since Lewis Hall against Fulham in January 2023 (also 14). Alonso’s side are outperforming the expected goals (13.34) metric by +5.56 (19 goals), the second best in the Premier League, while Sunderland are underperforming theirs (13.21) by -6.21, the second-worst performers. Chelsea have won 54.7 per cent of ground duels, the highest rate in the top flight. Only five teams have a lower pass completion rate this season than Sunderland (78.8 per cent). Chelsea (six) have found the net more times from set-plays in the league than any rival except Brighton (seven). The Blues (53) have managed the most shots on target in the Premier League, but also sustained the most by opponents (50). The Black Cats have not won at home in the top flight on this date since 1932, when they beat Grimsby 3-2. A year earlier, in a 2-0 defeat at Roker Park, Chelsea fielded our oldest-ever starting XI, averaging 31 years and 336 days.

news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has issued an update on the fitness of Moises Caicedo and Aaron Anselmino ahead of this weekend’s Premier League trip to Sunderland. The Blues manager confirmed earlier today (Friday) in his pre-match press conference that he will wait until after our final session tomorrow to make a call on Caicedo, who was absent from training earlier this week. Alonso said the Ecuadorian was feeling discomfort because of ‘little problems’ in the wake of our victory over Manchester United. The defender has yet to make his Chelsea debut, but there is a possibility that could change this weekend at the Stadium of Light. ‘He’s doing everything, and tomorrow [Saturday] we’ll decide, but he could be in the squad, yes,' said Alonso. Xabi Alonso: Every player will have their moment
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso is certain that every member of his Chelsea squad will make an impact on the team over the course of this season, believing it is key to make sure every player understands their next opportunity is never far away. Speaking in his pre-match press conference at Cobham on Friday, ahead of our Premier League trip to Sunderland, Alonso was asked whether it was challenging to manage his squad when every player is eager to play as big a role in the team as possible. The Spaniard’s side has seemed settled at times so far this season, but there are always tweaks to be made depending on our game plan and next opponent. Our manager was also quick to point out that the changing nature of form and fitness means any player’s next chance to stake a claim could be right around the corner at any time. ‘There are moments when a player feels that he's far from the pitch, but actually he's not that far,’ explained Alonso. ‘It's about having the opportunity. Everyone will have their moment. ‘We have seen it and we will see it happening again, because of the situations that we are having dealing with injuries in certain positions, some positions more than others. In the end, in the long run, you will see that everyone will play their role.’ Two examples the Blues manager pointed to are Estevao Willian and Wesley Fofana, who both started last week’s 2-0 win over Manchester United in the absence of Joao Pedro and Maxence Lacroix, who remain unavailable for the trip to the Stadium of Light. In the case of Estevao, Alonso felt it was an important moment for the young winger to come into the team and perform well, twice being unlucky to be denied a goal by narrow VAR calls against the Red Devils. ‘It was very good for him, for the team, that he had such an impact,’ our manager continued. ‘We had taken the decision and he knew that was going to be the game, and it was very important for him, that game, and for the team as well.’ Xabi also highlighted the growing maturity shown by Fofana, which he in part attributes to the 25-year-old becoming a father. Our French defender recovered from some first-half errors against Man Utd to play a key role in the brilliant second-half performance that secured all three points, earning praise for his mentality and resilience. ‘It's about dealing with difficult moments and he did many good things,' Alonso added. 'For sure, the mistakes, he knew and he reacted really well. The second half he was solid, he was reliable, as he was in Liverpool. ‘He's already been in the Premier League for years. He's been at this club for four years. It's part of the job to deal with some things that are not what you want, to deal with mistakes, to deal with difficult situations. ‘I'm seeing now Wes is very focused this year. He's mature - he's had his baby, so it's making him more mature - as well as taking more responsibility on the pitch. Sometimes he’s not direct, but sometimes that helps as well. So we support him and he's important.’

news.title: Bompastor delivers injury update on Lauren James and Lexi Potter
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has confirmed that Lauren James sustained a hamstring injury against Charlton, but there was more positive news about the fitness of Lexi Potter. The Blues sit top of the table following our 6-0 victory over Charlton last weekend, and are currently ahead of rivals Manchester City in second place on goal difference. The only disappointment for Chelsea fans during that emphatic win was that Lauren James was forced off with an injury after 35 minutes, with Erin Cuthbert drafted in to replace her as a substitute. And after having a full week to assess James' fitness, the head coach was able to give an update on her injury. 'LJ will be missing the games until the end of the block,' explained Bompastor. 'She had a scan, and she has an injury in her hamstring. We won’t see her on the pitch until the end of this block. 'Of course, we know how good Lauren is for us, for the team. My job is to make sure I find solutions when players are not available. The good thing is that I looked at some of the statistics we saw from last week, and we are a team who can score with different players. 'A lot of players were involved in the scoring against Charlton, and every player on the pitch had a shot on goal. Even if it was not always a great one, at least all of the players on the pitch had a shot on goal. That's a good thing. My job is to make sure I now find the solutions without LJ on the pitch.' Midfielder Lexi Potter missed out on the Charlton win with a small knee injury sustained against Roma in our 2-0 Women's Champions League victory, but has been training with the squad this week, as Bompastor explained. She said: 'We have Lexi Potter who is back in the squad and in contention for the game.' See the Blues in action against Everton at Stamford Bridge tomorrow! Tickets are available here...

news.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Sunderland
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says a decision on Emi Martinez's availability to face Sunderland will be taken tomorrow (Saturday), with the Blues manager also updating on the fitness of Moises Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix and Joao Pedro. After defeating Manchester United at Stamford Bridge last time out, the Blues are on the road this weekend as we make the long journey to Wearside to face a Sunderland side that have won one of their nine top-flight matches this season. Alonso will oversee our final pre-match training session tomorrow at Cobham, after which he will decide who starts against the Black Cats. One choice he may have to make is who starts in goal. Martinez has been sidelined since our win at Everton, after which he underwent jaw surgery, but has returned to training this week wearing protective headgear. ‘Tomorrow we have our last training session before Sunday and we will decide [if he is fit],' Alonso replied when asked about Martinez in his pre-match press conference. 'But he is training well.’ In Martinez's absence, Mike Penders has started our last three matches. And Alonso accepts he may face a difficult decision about who starts between the posts at the Stadium of Light. ‘All the decisions are tough, in all the positions. It is very good that Emi has made a great effort to be back and is ahead of the plan to be part of the team. So, tomorrow we will check and then on Sunday we will take the final decision.’ Alonso will also wait until after tomorrow's session to make a call on the fitness of Moises Caicedo, who was absent from training earlier in the week at Cobham. The Blues manager said: ‘He had little problems after the last game, so we expect to check tomorrow on different situations and Moi is one of them. It’s a discomfort, more than his calf.’ Three players who will definitely be absent this weekend are Hato, Lacroix and Joao Pedro, and Alonso stated that the trio will be assessed over the international break. ‘He isn’t fit yet,' Alonso said on Hato. 'It will take some more weeks. Not yet to be close, maybe after the international break but it’s going to take longer. 'After these two weeks of the international break, we will see how their recovery is and the progress they make. For sure, ahead of the Leeds game, I will have more of an update. But not today.’

news.title: PGA Division 1 report: Chelsea Women Under-18s 4-0 Sunderland
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women’s League, made it two wins from two in Division 1 with a 4-0 victory over Sunderland at Cobham. The Blues led inside three minutes through a Sunderland own goal, and Carla Gardiner doubled the advantage three minutes later. Chelsea N’Drin added a third before half-time, and Stevie Sinclair completed the scoring on 71 minutes. Leanne Champ’s side controlled possession and combined well to break down Sunderland and create good goalscoring chances. Positive attacking play was matched by solid defensive work, and the Blues kept a clean sheet. Chelsea led after three minutes. Gabi Storey found captain Belle Sullivan from a free-kick, and she played Rebekah Pierce in behind the Sunderland full-back. Pierce won back possession in the box and drove a cross towards goal, which deflected off a defender and spun under the goalkeeper. The lead was doubled three minutes later. Gardiner combined with Sinclair and Jahmya Putman across the top of the box before beating two defenders and firing a left-footed shot into the bottom corner. The third goal came on 39 minutes. Tess Finn and Sophie Leach worked the ball through midfield to Gardiner, who released Putman down the right. Putman’s ball across found Gardiner, whose first-time shot hit the post, and N’Drin reacted quickly to fire in the rebound. Champ made three changes at half-time, with Ella Booth, Keira Johnson and Aysia Matabaro replacing Zoe Ciccardini, Sullivan and Putman. Annie Boichat and Maria Mayers came on for Finn and N’Drin on the hour. The fourth goal came on 71 minutes. Youngsters Booth and Mayers combined with Leach, who played back to centre-back Boichat. Her long pass over the Sunderland left-back found Matabaro advancing down the right. Matabaro went one-on-one with the full-back and drove inside before slipping the ball through for Johnson, who had made a run behind the defence. Johnson found Sinclair in the six-yard box, and she finished first-time back across goal. Chelsea are unbeaten after our opening two Division 1 fixtures, scoring nine goals and conceding only one. The Blues return to PGA Cup action on Wednesday 11 November, when we host Ipswich Town in the first round at Cobham. Chelsea reached this stage with a 7-1 win over West Ham United in the preliminary round, and beat Ipswich 8-0 at Kingsmeadow when the sides met in the PGA South League in September. Chelsea: Victoria Rudz, Sophie Leach, Gabi Storey, Zoe Ciccardini (Ella Booth h-t), Belle Sullivan (c) (Keira Johnson HT), Tess Finn (Annie Boichat 60), Stevie Sinclair, Chelsea N’Drin (Maria Mayers 60), Rebekah Pierce, Carla Gardiner, Jahmya Putman (Aysia Matabaro h-t)Scorers: OG 3, Gardiner 6, N’Drin 39, Sinclair 71Manager: Leanne Champ

news.title: Bompastor and Blues quartet nominated for WSL awards
news.body_en: Two Blues have been nominated for the Women's Super League Player of the Month, Sonia Bompastor is up for the WSL Manager of the Month award, and fans can also vote for Keira Walsh and Maika Hamano to win the WSL Goal of the Month award. The head coach masterminded victories in all three of our league matches in October, first beating West Ham United 3-0 away from home, before returning to Stamford Bridge after the international break to deliver a stunning 6-2 victory over Tottenham Hotspur. Our final match of the month saw us come from behind to seal a 3-1 win against Crystal Palace at the 360 Engage Stadium in Sutton. Ellie Carpenter played every minute of those three matches, getting the crowd off their seats at the Bridge with an emphatic brace against Spurs. The wing-back put in standout performances across the month, working diligently in defence while also getting forward at every opportunity to contribute to the attack. Meanwhile, Chelsea striker Melvine Malard also had a superb month, netting three times. Her stunning goal from range against West Ham contributed to our 3-0 win, while her second-half brace against Palace helped turn the game around after the home side had taken the lead. Both Malard and Carpenter are up for Player of the Month, while Bompastor is in the running for the manager prize, which she has won on four occasions during her time with the Blues. Two outstanding goals from those three matches in October have been nominated for the WSL Goal of the Month award. The first comes from our win against the Hammers, where after receiving a sideways pass from Wieke Kaptein on the edge of the area, Walsh used her tried-and-tested technique from range to lash the ball into the bottom corner to the delight of the travelling fans. You can also vote for Hamano's swerving effort from 30 yards out when she netted against Spurs. The Japan international spent the second half of last season on loan with Martin Ho's side, but there was no room for sentiment when she got the Blues supporters out of their seats at Stamford Bridge with her superb strike. Voting for all three awards is now open and will close at 11am on Monday 9 November. The winners will be announced on Thursday 12 November. You can cast your vote for either Ellie or Melvine for Player of the Month by clicking here. Vote for Bompastor as Manager of the Month here, and either Keira or Maika for Goal of the Month here.

news.title: Chelsea attacker called up by England
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers has been named in the final England squad of 2026. The Chelsea attacker has been selected by Tuchel for the November international break, which follows our game against Sunderland on Sunday, following a superb start to the campaign for club and country. Rogers was a scorer in the last window, in the Three Lions’ big win in Croatia, and has since netted three times for the Blues, including in the recent victory over Manchester United. England have a pair of UEFA Nations League Group C fixtures that will determine whether they progress to next year’s knockout phase. The Three Lions currently sit second in the table with nine points from four matches. Tuchel’s side host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday 12 November, before travelling to Madrid to face top-of-the-table Spain on Sunday 15 November. That game is at the Metropolitano Stadium, the home of Atletico Madrid. At Under-21 level, meanwhile, Josh Acheampong has been selected in Lee Carsley's squad for a pair of friendlies against Portugal and France at Bristol City's Ashton Gate. England are preparing to defend their European Championship crown at next summer's tournament in Albania and Serbia. Tayo Subuloye, Jesse Derry and Shimmy Mheuka have all been named in the England Under-20 squad for their games against Czechia and Portugal, while the Blues quartet of Freddy Bernal, Landon Emenalo, Reggie Walsh and Chizaram Ezenwata have been called up by England Under-19s ahead of three European Championship qualifiers at that level. news.title: FPL 2026/27: Chelsea Gameweek 10
news.body_en: Chelsea have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. Here, we look at which Blues players are the best value-for-money picks, why Morgan Rogers (£8.1m) is Chelsea’s most popular player this week and who to captain in Gameweek 10. The deadline is at 6.30pm GMT on Friday ahead of Coventry City’s trip to Everton. Rogers is the most popular Chelsea player ahead of Gameweek 10 with over 200,000 transfers in. The Englishman netted his fifth goal of the season and claimed a share of the bonus against Man United, taking his total goal contributions in all competitions for Chelsea to ten (six goals and four assists). The attacker's ownership has reached 52 per cent, making Rogers the most-selected midfielder in Fantasy, and he has risen in price to £8.1m. In the last six Gameweeks, no Chelsea player has scored more points (31), while Rogers ranks joint-first for big chances (3), first for expected goals and second for expected goal involvement among Blues players. Also proving popular is Cole Palmer (£9.8m), who scored his first goal since Gameweek 2 from the penalty spot against Man United last time out. The Blues number 10 registered four shots on goal and created three chances for his team-mates. Palmer was also just one defensive contribution short of the required threshold for additional points. Since Gameweek 4, the England international has created five big chances, the second-most of any player. Sunderland’s underlying defensive data suggests Palmer will get plenty of opportunities on Sunday to build on his eight-point return from GW9. In the last six Gameweeks, the Black Cats have conceded a league-high 14 goals and rank second-worst for expected goals conceded. Josh Acheampong (£4.5m) continues to establish himself as a reliable, budget defender. The England Under-21 international started for the fourth consecutive Gameweek and picked up a nine-point return thanks to three bonus points, taking his points tally to 17 in three Gameweeks. Furthermore, Acheampong has produced defensive contribution points twice this season in six starts, and averages over seven DefCon per/90. Offensively, Estevao (£6.3m) caught the eye of many Fantasy managers against Man United, with the Brazilian unfortunate not to return. As well as having a well-taken goal narrowly ruled out for offside, Estevao racked up a match-high six shots, 12 penalty box touches and three chances created. The teenager was the cheapest Chelsea attacker to start in GW9. If he can retain his place in the team going forward, Estevao could be a superb differential in FPL. Erling Haaland (£15.8m) is once again a safe captaincy choice for Man City’s away trip to Nottingham Forest. The Norwegian has scored nine goals in the last eight Gameweeks, racking up 66 Fantasy points in that time with two double-digit hauls and 14 bonus points. No player has had more shots on target or xGI than the league’s top-scorer, while Forest have kept just one clean sheet and are winless since Gameweek four. Elsewhere, Alexander Isak (£9.2m) is an intriguing differential option against Crystal Palace. The Eagles have conceded a league-high 31 big chances in nine matches. The Liverpool forward has been bought by over 200,000 managers ahead of the deadline and has scored six goals, only Haaland has more. Isak ranks third among all forwards for xG with 4.35 and shots on target with nine.

news.title: Sunderland vs Chelsea: Key statistics and facts
news.body_en: Chelsea head to Sunderland on Sunday looking to make it back-to-back victories in the Premier League. Here are all the key facts and figures you need ahead of kick-off. Chelsea’s win against Manchester United on matchweek nine moved us into the top four in the Premier League table. Sunday’s opponents Sunderland are bottom, with one win and two draws so far. This fixture has seen 124 goals scored in 34 Premier League matches, averaging 3.65 goals per game. Our last victory at the Stadium of Light came in December 2016, when a goal from Cesc Fabregas just before half-time earned us a 1-0 win. We have played there only once since. In the home match in 2016/17, Chelsea won 5-1. Last season’s defeat on the last day of the season was only our second in 14 Premier League visits to the Stadium of Light, where we have recorded 10 wins and two draws. Chelsea are aiming to prevent the Black Cats recording a third consecutive league victory against us for the first time since a run of three between 1999 and 2001. Played: 127Won: 61Drawn: 22Lost: 44 17 December 2013 | League Cup L 2-1 aet | Lampard29 November 2014 | Premier League D 0-07 May 2016 | Premier League L 3-2 | Diego Costa, Matic14 December 2016 | Premier League W 1-0 | Fabregas24 May 2026 | Premier League L 2-1 | Palmer Chelsea 7-2 Sunderland | 2009/10 | Premier LeagueSunderland 4-0 Chelsea | 1909/10, 1912/13, 1934/35 | Division OneChelsea's biggest win at Sunderland was 4-2 in the 2010/11 Premier League. news.title: Carlo Cudicini interview: Sunderland saves, penalty record and personal honour
news.body_en: With the 25th anniversary of a legendary performance from Carlo Cudicini away to Sunderland approaching, we caught up with the former Chelsea goalkeeper ahead of this weekend's visit to Wearside... Earlier this year, Carlo Cudicini was asked a simple question that was far from easy to answer. ‘What was your best performance in a Chelsea shirt?’ The passage of time dictates that memories fade, but those that linger burn the brightest. You could almost see Cudicini whirring through his 200-plus games for the Blues, from his debut in August 1999 to his final appearance for us nearly ten years later. Eventually, he settled on a ‘game at Sunderland, a goalless draw’. For a man who represented Chelsea with such distinction – in high-profile Premier League games, FA Cup finals, Champions League classics – a 0-0 at the Stadium of Light on a wintry December afternoon might be considered an inauspicious response. Watch back the highlights, though, and you get the sense of a goalkeeper at the very top of his game. Kevin Phillips, one of the Premier League’s top strikers at the turn of the century, is denied on three occasions, including from the penalty spot followed by an improbable save with the Italian’s feet from a few yards out. ‘It was probably related more to feeling than anything else,’ Cudicini, now Chelsea’s head of talent and pathways, tells us at Cobham this week when we enquire about that Sunderland performance. ‘Most of the time, a player or a keeper’s performance is just judged on whether he scores or saves, but I think it’s more related to what the feeling was during the game. And that day, there was just no way they were scoring a goal. ‘That was the feeling I probably developed throughout the game, after making the first save. It’s all about momentum. And as well I loved to play away, because you get the feeling the opponents keep coming, you keep saving, and the supporters get frustrated because it’s like going up against a wall.’ Cudicini can recall only a handful of occasions throughout his career when he felt truly unbeatable. The Sunderland game 25 years ago was one of them, and an important factor behind Cudicini’s inner belief that he would not concede was the way he got in Phillips’ head. ‘A big part of being a goalkeeper is the psychological battle with the striker, without a doubt,’ Cudicini explains. ‘If on one side you feel unbeatable, on the other you frustrate the striker who can only say: “What do I have to do?” ‘That gets in their mind. They can overthink it and there’s a component in there saying: “Maybe I’m trying too hard to score.”’ Cudicini remembers a sense of personal pride and satisfaction with his performance at the Stadium of Light, but in the context of the season, it was two points dropped. Claudio Ranieri’s Blues had aspirations of finishing in the top four. Unfortunately, inconsistency continued to plague us. A week prior to the Sunderland game, we took the champions Manchester United apart at Old Trafford, a clinic of counter-attacking football securing a famous 3-0 success. But that was followed by a 1-0 loss at home to lowly Charlton, and then the goalless draw on Wearside. The next weekend, we thrashed top-of-the-table Liverpool 4-0. Cudicini saved yet another penalty in that game, this time from Gary McAllister. His stop from Darren Bent’s spot-kick the following April means he is a member of an exclusive club to have saved a record three penalties in a single Premier League season. ‘Obviously you need a bit of luck, but there were probably two main points to my penalty record,’ reflects Cudicini, who would deny Ruud van Nistelrooy and Thierry Henry from 12 yards later in his Chelsea career. ‘One was my characteristics as a goalkeeper. Not being the tallest meant I was very elastic, very springy, very reactive, and with penalties you need that, because a centimetre can be the difference. ‘At the same time, I did a lot of research at a time when we didn’t have data, like a goalkeeper coach coming in the day before the match saying, “Those are where he took the last ten penalties”. I played at the wrong time for that! ‘I started the work during pre-season, watching every friendly where a lot of times it finished with penalties. I would take notes. Then, during the season, I would watch every episode of Match of the Day, looking at the penalties, what minute they were in, the scoreline, where it was going. ‘So I was going into games having my philosophy around that, based on research I had done, and that year it worked brilliantly.’ The 2001/02 campaign culminated with Cudicini becoming just the fourth goalkeeper to win the Chelsea Player of the Season award. That was no mean feat, partly because Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Eidur Gudjohnsen formed a deadly strike partnership that year, scoring a remarkable 52 goals between them. Not only that, but Cudicini didn’t actually establish himself in the Chelsea starting XI until two weeks before the draw at Sunderland. A pre-season injury handed Ed de Goey a place back between the posts on the opening day, and then when the Dutchman’s form dipped, Ranieri turned to Mark Bosnich. It wasn’t until he tore a thigh muscle late on in a goalless draw at Goodison Park that Cudicini was handed his chance. It was one he grabbed with both hands, registering six clean sheets in his first seven games back, not least because of that pair of penalty saves in consecutive weeks. ‘I was disappointed because I thought I’d done enough the season before to start again when I was fit. Mark had a couple of good games, so I understood that, but I was disappointed. ‘I was training very well and thinking that surely it had to change. As a goalkeeper, you either play or you don’t. You can’t come on for 20 minutes. But when Mark got injured, I stepped in. That’s how it works for goalkeepers. ‘I remember I had such huge energy after the Everton game. I came on for Mark and made a good save right at the end to keep it 0-0. All that frustration at not playing built up, and then that good energy and good feeling from the game brought me momentum.’ Cudicini’s presence between the posts proved pivotal in the Blues securing a sixth-placed finish and with it, European football for the following campaign. We did well in the domestic cups, too, reaching the semi-finals of the League Cup and then the final of the FA Cup. Alas, our north London rivals put paid to our hopes of silverware, but our No.23 did still end the season with a trophy in his hands. ‘The Player of the Year didn’t exist at that time in Italy,’ Cudicini says. ‘I remember my first year when I joined Chelsea, and there was the Player of the Year, and I was asking Roberto [Di Matteo], Gianfranco [Zola], obviously Italian guys: "What is this all about?” ‘They explained to me, so I understood its importance. So when I was awarded one, it was a great honour. I was really proud of the relationship that I managed to build with the fans. ‘Personally, that season was probably the most important in my career at Chelsea,' adds Cudicini. 'Coming from Castel di Sangro for £150,000, being alone, not playing at the start, it was all the build-up to that season. ‘A lot of it was down to my relationship with the fans, I think. Coming from Italy, you're passionate, so you get agitated, you get upset, you celebrate with the fans. That was the bond we had.’ As much as memories fade, the image of Cudicini clenching his fists and roaring with joy after saving a penalty will live in Chelsea supporters’ minds for a long while yet.

news.title: Melvine Malard on why there's even more to come from her at Chelsea
news.body_en: Melvine Malard has hit the ground running at Chelsea. Our new number nine has scored eight goals in seven starts and three substitute appearances since signing from Manchester United this summer. Little wonder, then, she is our top scorer so far. Last season, she netted six times in 21 league outings for the Red Devils, but she has now equalled that tally in her first six WSL games with Chelsea. When we sit down with the France international, we mention how her strike rate has so clearly improved. We then ask her what she attributes her good form to, but her answer comes as a surprise. Six goals in six league games, and Malard feels we haven't seen anything yet. ‘I don’t think I’m in my good form yet; that’s the thing,’ she says with a huge smile. ‘Not yet. ‘When you play with a lot of quality individuals, it can help you a lot. Having a positive vibe in your head can also help you a lot. I just need to keep going to reach my top form. ‘What I understand more now with the number nine role is you need to have a lot of patience, and you need to be ready in the box when players give you the ball.’ Malard has settled in so quickly to life at Chelsea. She talks about positivity, and she certainly brings the vibes around the training ground and on the pitch. The time has flown since her arrival in July, and she gives us some insight into the team’s hectic schedule and how she stays focused on the task in front of her. ‘It’s busy, very busy,’ she explains. ‘We play a lot of games with big intensity against a lot of quality players, so it’s busy but very good. ‘When you play well, you feel good, and you win. Also, you score goals. That's my job. I’m very happy to be here and to be doing my job at the moment. I’m taking it game by game. We have a lot of matches, with the Champions League and the national team and everything like that. ‘My job is to help the team when I can: to take responsibility, and take the opportunities I have in front of goal and don’t overthink things. If you make sure you play with passion, you enjoy your football and score the goals. ‘You can see that many people can score in this team, so I don’t worry about it. With good team-mates around you, you know you can have a lot of opportunities, a lot of action in front of goal and okay, if you miss that one, the next player will give you another ball to try again.’ Malard played for Sonia Bompastor from the age of 14. After making the move from her home on the island of La Reunion in the Indian Ocean to play for Lyon, she is now in her second spell under Bompastor and details how the head coach has evolved since then. ‘Sonia is the same,’ she says. ‘The same coach demanding a lot. She’s very exigent with you and your quality. But it’s good to have a coach that pushes you a lot and makes sure you don’t become complacent. ‘She’s maybe a little bit more relaxed here. She shows more happiness. We know in England it’s very free, so she can speak her mind. It’s good to feel free.’ This Saturday sees Chelsea host Everton at Stamford Bridge in the WSL. When we ask her what we can expect, the striker pauses and gives us a thoughtful answer on what a fast start could mean for her team-mates. It’s evident she cares very much about the collective. ‘Everton also have good players, good quality,’ she says when asked about the opposition. ‘They play direct, and when they have the opportunity to shoot, they are not scared to do it, no matter who is in front of them. 'We need to make sure we are always focused on every ball and every player. We want to score quickly. We saw against Charlton that when we score quickly in the first half, we can also allow other players to enjoy the game, like Giulia (Dragoni). 'When she scored her first, she had a lot of emotion because the team did their jobs in the first half and gave her the chance to show her football. If we can do that in every game, it's good for our team, and everyone is happy.' Malard isn’t the kind of player who wants to talk at length about individual accolades. When we ask her about attending last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony, she once again relates being ranked 28th in the world to how it rewarded the most important people in her life. ‘It was amazing,’ she says. ‘You sacrifice a lot in your life to become a footballer, so it’s special when you are nominated. I went with my wife and my mum. It was a big thank you very much for all the help they have given me in my life. ‘But we need to keep going to be nominated again. Because football is not easy. I went to the ceremony, but now it’s done. We need to move on and keep working hard. ‘I’d like to get higher up the list, but there is a lot of talent so the places are tight. You just need to keep doing your best.’ See Melvine and the Blues in action against Everton at Stamford Bridge on Saturday! Tickets are available here...

news.title: October Chelsea Goal of the Month winner revealed!
news.body_en: For the second month in a row, Morgan Rogers has received the Chelsea Goal of the Month award. Since joining the Blues from Aston Villa in the summer, Rogers has now won two of the three Goal of the Month awards available, including the last two in a row. That has come during a brilliant start to his Chelsea career, which has seen him become the first Blues player – and only the second across the entire Premier League – to reach ten goal involvements (six goals, four assists) in all competitions this season. His two award-winning goals showed very different qualities, too. In September, it was for his instinctive volley into the bottom corner from the edge of the box away at Arsenal. This time around, he finished top of the October poll thanks to his opener against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, taking the ball from Romeo Lavia near the centre-circle and driving forward through the heart of the defence and into the box, before lifting a composed finish over the keeper. It was a tight race for the October Goal of the Month award, though. Jordan Henderson’s first Chelsea goal, swept in against Bournemouth, came second with 34 per cent of the votes, while the midfielder’s free-kick scored later in the same game was a distant third. However, it is Rogers who triumphs for the second month in a row by receiving 39 per cent of supporters’ votes on the Chelsea Official App.

news.title: Chelsea loan report: Essugo, Murray-Campbell and Samuels-Smith impress
news.body_en: Chelsea's players out on loan continued their development across Europe and the English football pyramid during October, with several making important contributions for their temporary clubs. We take a look at how the Blues' loanees performed during the month, with Dario Essugo, Harrison Murray-Campbell and Ishe Samuels-Smith among those catching the eye. Dario Essugo started each of Strasbourg’s three games in October, deployed in the centre of the Ligue 1 side’s midfield. He scored the opening goal, his first for the club, in Strasbourg’s 2-1 defeat to Nice, while also playing the full 90 minutes against European champions Paris Saint-Germain. Genesis Antwi and Filip Jorgensen continue to provide a strong contribution with both also starting all three games. Samuels-Smith continued his impressive development at Notts County, featuring in five matches across League One and the EFL Trophy. He completed the full 90 minutes in four of those appearances, including the victories over Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest’s Under-21s, and demonstrated his versatility by featuring at centre-back and on the left of midfield. Murray-Campbell (pictured top) remains an important member of RC Kortrijk’s defence in his first loan spell in senior football. The 20-year-old played in the games against Genk and Standard Liege, with Kortrijk earning a hard-fought point away from home in the latter. October saw Derry make his debut appearance in the UEFA Champions League during the Portuguese side's 2-0 win away to Lens. The winger provided an assist for Sporting Lisbon in their 2-1 victory over Maritimo in the quarter-finals of the Portuguese League Cup. Wilson has been an ever-present for Rochdale this season, with the highlight of his October a clean sheet kept in a battling 1-0 success over Swindon Town at the start of the month. Seventeen-year-old Kavuma-McQueen enjoyed another productive month with Portsmouth, featuring in six Championship fixtures during October. The young winger made his presence felt particularly in the 3-2 victory over Sheffield United, claiming an assist as Pompey secured an important three points. Walsh continues to gain valuable senior experience at Wigan Athletic, featuring in all six of the League One side's October fixtures. He provided an assist in their game against Huddersfield and started both the Latics’ victories during the month, against Reading and Barrow. Emenalo made his senior debut in October as Celtic beat Hearts 7-1. He followed that up by featuring in the draw with Dundee United. Mhueka was also involved in all three Scottish Premiership fixtures. Satpayev returned to action during October following an injury that restricted his involvement in September. The 18-year-old made three appearances for Burnley, taking his total to seven since joining the Championship club on loan. It was an excellent month for Sarr and Real Sociedad. The defender started each of their six fixtures, with four of those won, including three in La Liga. Those victories have seen them rise to fifth in the table. They also picked up their maiden Europa League victory of the campaign, thrashing Lillestrom 6-0 away from home. Having returned from suspension, Disasi started Palace’s Premier League games against Newcastle and Tottenham towards the end of the month. He also played the full 90 minutes in the Eagles’ Europa League fixtures away to Lyon and Besiktas. Badiashile started four matches for Napoli in the heart of defence, including a Champions League defeat at Villarreal and a thrilling 3-3 draw with Roma. Unfortunately, an injury sustained in that game has ruled him out of Napoli’s past two fixtures. Sanchez played twice for Como, starting their Champions League defeat to Feyenoord and 3-1 Serie A victory over Torino. Garnacho saw more involvement for Villa in October, coming off the bench in four games including the Champions League successes at home to Fenerbahce and Viking Stavanger. Harrison has firmly established himself in Wimbledon’s midfield, starting six of their seven appearances in a busy October. He accumulated more than 300 minutes of football in the process. Richards, meanwhile, is currently sidelined through injury. Kiano Dyer continues to feature regularly for Chesterfield in League Two. He made five appearances for the Spireites, who are currently positioned in tenth place. It was a flawless October for Boreham Wood and Curd, who came into the team at the start of the month. He subsequently played each of their five National League games - all of which were won – and kept two clean sheets in the process. They are already 12 points clear at the top of the table. Merrick was in the opposition goal as Boreham Wood won a dramatic game against Hartlepool 4-3 this past weekend. It was the young keeper’s second appearance of the month, following a 2-1 success against Hornchurch. Sands continues to feature regularly between the posts for Dulwich in the Isthmian Premier League, making four appearances as the south London side sit just outside the play-off positions.

news.title: What kit are Chelsea wearing against Sunderland?
news.body_en: Chelsea's final game before the November international break takes us to the North-East of England to play Sunderland. The Blues head to the Stadium of Light fresh off the 2-0 success against Manchester United last weekend. We also won our most recent Premier League away game, at Everton, and another victory on Sunday will ensure we go into the last international break of 2026 in the top four. Our opponents, meanwhile, will be aiming to pick up their second league win of the season and move off the foot of the Premier League table. We can confirm the Blues will be wearing our 2026/27 Nike away kit for the second time this season, having previously worn the shirt in the game at Brentford in September. Our away strip mirrors many of the features of the home shirt on a black base, with the same Midwest Gold trim and laurel wreath motif appearing prominently around the neck and cuffs, as well as the golden socks.
